Choose whether to show remaining charge and whether “Current state” prefers average battery current. Current is always measured when available. The multiplier corrects current and calculated power throughout the app; logs retain the original instantaneous current so the multiplier can be changed later.
Display the device-reported remaining battery charge in mAh?

Some devices report unexpected units or signs. Multiply the reported value here to correct the displayed result.\n \n As a rough phone reference, Android’s standard sign is positive while charging and negative while discharging. Active charging is often around +500 to +5000 mA, while ordinary discharge is often around -100 to -3000 mA. Values near zero can be normal when the battery is nearly full or the phone is idle. If the magnitude looks about 1000 times too small or too large, or the sign is reversed, adjust the multiplier.
Automatic detection is unavailable for the current battery state or reading
Use the recent average on “Current state” when available?

Some devices provide a recent average in addition to instantaneous current. The averaging period varies by device. “Current state” uses instantaneous current when the average is unavailable. This option applies only to “Current state”; logs always store the original instantaneous reading.

This estimate uses the configured Battery Monitor predictor. Its target does not control charging or shutdown.
Choose how remaining time is calculated and which battery levels it targets

Choose how Battery Monitor estimates remaining time and the target battery levels. Targets also apply to “Charging target reached” and “Discharging target reached” alarms. Battery Monitor does not start or stop charging.

“Sensitive” uses the recent five-minute rate. “Conservative”, the default, combines recent rates with the learned long-term average to reduce sudden changes. “Since Status Change” uses the current charging or discharging session. “Long-term Average” uses the learned rate for discharge or the active charging source. Until enough observations are available, estimates use the stored average or an initial default.

“Automatic” uses a fixed device charging target when Battery Monitor can read one, and otherwise uses 100%. Adaptive charging still targets 100%. “Custom” uses your chosen level for charging estimates and “Charging target reached” alarms.

Automatic detection may work on Google Pixel, Samsung Galaxy, Xiaomi/Redmi/POCO, OnePlus/Oppo/Realme, and Sony Xperia devices, and on devices running GrapheneOS or LineageOS—particularly when root or Shizuku access is available. It relies on software signals, so availability and accuracy are not guaranteed even for the listed manufacturers. Untested models or OS versions in these families may also work, but devices from other manufacturers are not currently detected automatically.

Devices come in all shapes and sizes, so most translations need to use abbreviations to ensure that the time-remaining estimate fits comfortably in the notification area. If it still doesn\'t fit, you can opt for the “Condensed” format. If you have plenty of room, you might prefer the “Verbose” setting.

All eight alarm types are always available. Switch events on directly, or use “Add threshold” under a charge or temperature type. New thresholds are enabled after saving. Tap a value to edit it; editing keeps its on/off state. Disabled values remain listed. “Delete alarm” asks for confirmation. Sound and vibration are shared by type in Android notification settings. Existing duplicate records appear as one logical alarm; switching or deleting affects all copies. Charging and discharging alarms follow estimate targets and do not control charging. A blocked channel or stopped monitor does not change saved switches.
A system-reported battery problem, not a capacity-health percentage
This is where you can control what conditions trigger the alarm.

For charge and temperature alarms, set the threshold and save the rule. The alarm fires when a reading reaches or passes the threshold in the chosen direction. Repeated readings at the threshold do not repeat the alarm. Starting the monitor, importing a rule or enabling it beyond the threshold does not fire it immediately; a later crossing is required.

Save battery observations and status changes for “History”. Available measurements include level, temperature, voltage, original instantaneous current, and remaining charge. Power is calculated from voltage and current when displayed or exported; it is not stored separately. Turning logging off does not erase existing history or stop time estimates.

When logging is enabled, connecting to power removes logs older than this limit. “Never delete” keeps them until you clear them manually. If automatic export is enabled, Battery Monitor exports pending logs before deleting old entries; a failed export prevents that deletion.
Periodically save new logs to a folder

Configure automatic export in “Settings” → “Advanced”. Choose a folder, frequency, format, and whether to create separate files or append to one file. Exports normally save logs since the previous automatic export; a new ongoing file includes all available logs. Android may delay exports while idle. Logging must remain enabled.

CSV is useful in a spreadsheet or text editor. It includes the original current, remaining charge, and power calculated using the multiplier selected at export time. JSON preserves structured log data for backups. Unavailable current, remaining charge, and power cells remain empty.

Unrestricted background execution can improve monitoring reliability. Android battery optimization may delay updates and alerts.\n \n Allowing unrestricted background execution may increase background battery use. You can change this later in Android “Settings” → “Apps” → “Battery Monitor” → “Battery”. Menu names vary by device.
Start Battery Monitor when device boots:

“Always” starts background monitoring after a device restart. “Never” skips the automatic start at boot. “If running on shutdown” follows whether you last started or stopped monitoring in Battery Monitor. Closing the app or ending its process does not count as stopping monitoring. Widgets do not override this choice.
Fine-tune Battery Monitor with additional controls for specialized use cases

Control privileged access, history logging, log retention, and automatic exports. “Background monitoring” opens checks and tools for permissions, monitor reliability, and debug logs. Open “OEM charging-target diagnostics” for charging-target reports.
Use granted root or Shizuku access for more complete and accurate device data?

Enable additional device readings through root or Shizuku access that you grant. When Android cannot provide a supported value, Battery Monitor also uses these readings on “Current state” and in logs. Extra diagnostics are collected automatically; there is no separate switch for advanced statistics.

“Diagnostics” combines monitor reliability, saved predictor data and battery data in “App operation”, “Battery”, “Charging” and “Raw” tabs. Android data is available without root. Extra device data depends on the device and permissions available to Battery Monitor.

Battery readings are labeled and formatted as remaining charge in mAh, current in mA, energy in mWh, voltage in V, temperature in your selected unit, and power in W. The current multiplier also applies to calculated power. Average current and cycle count depend on device support.

“Capacity” shows full-charge capacity, design capacity, and estimated health. Estimated health is calculated as full-charge capacity divided by design capacity, so it is only as accurate as the values reported by the device.
Reported full capacity exceeds design capacity. A reliable health estimate cannot be calculated from these readings.

“Charging” shows values related to the active charging path, such as maximum charging current or voltage, charging policy, charging state, and capacity level. These fields may change between chargers and charging modes.

“Raw” includes original names and values from Android battery broadcasts and, when accessible, dumpsys battery. These can include charging source, battery status, temperature, voltage, and other battery-service state.

“Raw” shows the original names and values read from /sys/class/power_supply, including multiline values. Search by key and tap a row to view and copy its complete value. Use “Refresh” to collect new readings. Battery Monitor also tries reads with its normal Android permissions, without root or Shizuku.

“Raw” also includes original BatteryManager property names and values, including available counters and current readings. Additional properties such as manufacturing details or replacement status depend on Android version, device support, and permissions.

Android data is collected automatically in “Diagnostics”. For additional root or Shizuku data, enable privileged access under “Additional sources”. Battery Monitor tries root first, then Shizuku. Shizuku must be running and permission granted. Missing fields remain unavailable; failed refreshes retain the previous snapshot and mark it stale.
Check permissions, monitoring reliability, and create a report for troubleshooting

“Background monitoring” checks permissions and monitor reliability. Use its controls to start or stop monitoring, change debug logging, open battery optimization and notification settings, or create a troubleshooting report. Not every unavailable reading indicates a permission problem; some devices do not provide it.

Check notification permission, root or Shizuku access, the monitoring service and the history database. Tap a check to request access or test it. “Start monitoring” is available while stopped; “Stop monitoring” is available while running. Device support and granted access determine which readings are available. The service check needs monitoring to be running; the database check needs history logging (“Settings” → “Advanced”). To use additional readings, enable “Use privileged access” in “Settings” → “Advanced”. “Manufacturer settings” is available only on supported devices.

Average current is a separate device reading from instantaneous current. Battery Monitor does not calculate its own average when the device provides none.
This estimate needs positive full-charge and design capacities from the same battery. Full-charge capacity must not exceed design capacity.
This is the charging estimate reported by the device. “Current state” uses Battery Monitor’s configured prediction method and can show an estimate even when no device estimate is available.
Rates show the time for one percentage point. Recent calculations are kept in memory; saved averages survive a restart. Incomplete windows use the long-term rate, and unsaved averages use defaults.

“App operation” shows saved long-term averages and the recent predictor inputs. Recent rates use changes in battery percentage and show the time for one percentage point, the selected method, the active charging source, observed points and durations, and whether the unfinished interval is included. The five-minute and five-point windows use the active long-term rate for unobserved portions; skipped levels are interpolated. Recent state is kept in memory and resets when monitoring restarts, switches between charging and discharging, or the charging source changes. Saved learned averages survive a restart. This data is independent of history logs; clearing logs does not reset estimates.

Capture at least two different OEM charging modes first
Delete locally stored OEM charging snapshots

1. Unplug the phone and keep it disconnected while capturing configuration snapshots. Change only the OEM charging protection setting between snapshots.
 2. Turn charging protection off, wait 2–5 seconds, then capture a snapshot.
 3. Select any fixed charging target, wait 2–5 seconds, and capture another snapshot. Repeat with at least one different fixed charging target if available.
 4. Enable adaptive, smart, or scheduled charging, wait 2–5 seconds, and capture one more snapshot.
 5. If the configuration comparison is inconclusive, you may optionally repeat the sequence while charging to capture runtime-only state.
 6. Create and review the comparison report. Report data is filtered and potentially sensitive values are redacted, but you should still review the complete report before sharing it.
After reviewing the report, copy or save it and send it by email to tomasz@swistak.codes.
Back up, restore, and transfer your app settings and battery data

Save and restore settings, alarms, logs, and learned prediction data. “Restore default settings” resets app preferences after confirmation while keeping history, alarms, learned estimates, and whether monitoring is running.
A general backup saves settings, alarms, and device-specific data together. When restoring it, you can choose which available data to import.

Import logs from a CSV exported by Battery Monitor and choose whether to add them or replace existing logs. Older exports may not contain current or remaining charge; those measurements stay empty for older entries. JSON backups preserve the structured data and are preferable for restoring it.
CSV formats can differ between app versions, so the import may not always work correctly.
